During the 2022 World Cup Round of 16 match between Morocco and Spain, Achraf Hakimi scored a decisive Panenka penalty to secure Morocco's victory in the penalty shootout.  The match ended 0-0 after 120 minutes, leading to a penalty shootout. Hakimi, born in Spain but representing Morocco, stepped up to take the crucial penalty. He calmly executed a Panenka, dinking the ball down the middle of the goal, deceiving the Spanish goalkeeper Unai Simon and sealing Morocco's place in the quarterfinals.  Morocco won the penalty shootout 3-0, with Spain missing all three of their attempts. Hakimi's penalty, described as nerveless and outrageous, sparked wild celebrations among the Moroccan players and fans, marking a historic moment for the team. It was a particularly poignant moment for Hakimi, scoring against the country of his birth to send his parents' homeland into the next round of the World Cup.  This victory marked the first time Morocco had reached the World Cup quarterfinals, making them the first Arab nation to achieve this feat.
